questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to express policy-as-code for security/compliance in multi-cloud clusters, combining network isolation, identity controls, and outbound security.

## Key Concepts
- Gatekeeper/OPA ConstraintTemplate
- NetworkPolicy as runtime guard
- Pod securityContext and automountServiceAccountToken control
- mTLS and central CA validation for outbound traffic
- CI verification using kubectl, gatekeeper audits

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8snetworkidentity
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sNetworkIdentityConstraint
  targets:
  - target: Kubernetes
    rego: |
      package k8snetworkidentity
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind == "Deployment"
        not has_ns_deny_ingress(input)
        msg := "Deployment namespace must have a deny-ingress NetworkPolicy and allow only whitelisted sources."
      }
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest (no deny ingress and automount enabled)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: example-fail
  namespace: dev
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: example-fail
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: example-fail
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:alpine
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest (deny ingress, trusted SA, automount disabled)
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: app-sa
  namespace: dev
  annotations:
    trusted.example.io: "true"
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: example-pass
  namespace: dev
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: example-pass
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: example-pass
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: app-sa
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:alpine
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
```

```yaml
# Minimal NetworkPolicy (deny ingress by default, allow from trusted namespace)
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-ingress
  namespace: dev
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  ingress:
  - from:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          env: trusted
```

## CI Verification Steps
- Gatekeeper audit run in CI to ensure constraints are evaluated.
- kubectl apply --dry-run=client -f failing.yaml should trigger policy violations.
- kubectl apply -f passing.yaml should succeed and Gatekeeper should record no violations.
- Validate that namespaces have the required NetworkPolicy objects and that deployments use trusted SAs with automountServiceAccountToken disabled.

## Why This Is Asked
This task tests practical CI gating for container hygiene: linting with Hadolint and enforcing image tagging discipline across manifests.

## Key Concepts
- Hadolint integration in GitHub Actions
- YAML parsing to inspect image tags
- Regular expressions for pinning (no latest, no -dev) and clear failure messages
- Practical debugging of lint vs. policy failures

## Code Example
```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci-docker-k8s.yml
name: CI Gate: Dockerfile lint + tag pin
on:
  push:
    branches: [ main, master ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ '**' ]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: hadolint/hadolint-action@v3
        with:
          dockerfile: '**/Dockerfile'
      - name: Check pinned image tags
        run: |
          set -e
          if grep -RIn 'image:.*:.*(latest|dev.*)' manifests || true; then
            echo 'Unpinned image tag detected' ; exit 1;
          fi
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you scale this gate to many repos?
- How would you extend checks for other tag policies (sha256 digests)?

# Istio AuthorizationPolicy (compliant example)
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: mongodb-per-tenant-access
  namespace: tenantA
spec:
  action: ALLOW
  rules:
  - from:
    - source:
        principals: ["spiffe://cluster/tenantA/pod-1"]
    to:
    - operation:
        ports: ["27017"]
```

```yaml
# Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate (pseudo)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sspiffe
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: SPIFFEIsTenantScoped
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package k8sspiffe
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"

questions.explanation:
Why This Is Asked
- Tests ability to translate governance requirements into concrete, enforceable policies and CI steps. 
- Combines data catalog metadata with image provenance and basic security gates in a beginner-friendly way.

Key Concepts
- Policy as code (Kyverno/OPA Gatekeeper)
- Annotations for data governance (data-catalog.uri)
- Image provenance (digest pinning, registry allowlist)
- Basic hardening (forbidden hostNetwork/hostPath, non-privileged)
- Namespace quotas and network policies

Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: Policy
metadata:
  name: governance-baseline
spec:
  rules:
  - name: require-data-catalog
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment", "StatefulSet"]
    validate:
      message: "data.catalog.uri annotation required"
      pattern:
        metadata:
          annotations:
            data.catalog.uri: "?*"
  - name: require-image-digest
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment", "StatefulSet"]
    validate:
      message: "image must be pinned with digest"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - image: "*@sha256:*"
  - name: disallow-risky-fields
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Pod", "Deployment", "StatefulSet"]
    prune: false
    validate:
      message: "hostNetwork/hostPath/privileged not allowed"
      pattern:
        spec:
          hostNetwork: False
        volumes: []
```

kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: data-processor

        - name: processor
          image: registry.internal/data-processor:latest
```

Passing Manifest (example)

              memory: "128Mi"

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates real-world expertise in supply chain security by testing the ability to tie SBOMs to runtime admission policies. It aligns with vendor-agnostic security frameworks (SLSA, SBOM) and modern GitOps deployment patterns where provenance verification is critical.

## Key Concepts

- **CycloneDX SBOMs**: Standardized software bills of materials that document container contents
- **Image digests**: SHA256 references ensuring immutable image pinning
- **Kyverno admission control**: Policy engine validating deployments at Kubernetes admission time
- **Helm chart provenance**: Ensuring charts reference verified, SBOM-backed images

## Proposed Solution

### GitHub Actions Workflow: Generate and Publish SBOMs

```yaml
name: SBOM Pipeline
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  build-and-sbom:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
      - uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - uses: anchore/sbom-action@v0
        with:
          format: cyclonedx-json
          image: ${{ github.repository }}
          output-file: sbom.json
      - run: |
          echo "${{ steps.sbom.outputs.sbom-json }}" | ghcr.io/your-org/sbom-store:latest 
            --image=${{ github.repository }}@${{ steps.build.outputs.digest }}
```

### Kyverno Policy: Enforce SBOM Presence at Admission

```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-image-sbom
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  background: true
  rules:
  - name: validate-sbom-present
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
        - Deployment
        - StatefulSet
        - DaemonSet
    preconditions:
      any:
      - key: "{{ request.operation }}"
        operator: In
        value: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
    validate:
      message: "All container images must have an associated CycloneDX SBOM"
      foreach:
      - list: "{{ request.object.spec.template.spec.containers[] }}"
        deny:
          conditions:
          - key: "{{ element.image }}"
            operator: NotEqual
            value: ""
          - key: "{{ lookup('sbom.verify', '{{ element.image }}', 'cyclonedx') }}"
            operator: NotEqual
            value: "valid"
```

### Failing Manifest (No SBOM)

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: vulnerable-app
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: vulnerable-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: vulnerable-app
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:1.25
```

**Expected Result**: Deployment blocked with error: "All container images must have an associated CycloneDX SBOM"

### Passing Manifest (SBOM Verified)

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: verified-app
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: verified-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: verified-app
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app

## Why This Is Asked
This question demonstrates end-to-end supply chain security expertise: image signing, SBOM provenance tracking, CVE scanning, and runtime verification in a multi-cloud, high-stakes environment. It tests knowledge of Sigstore ecosystem tools and policy enforcement.

- Image signing with Cosign/Sigstore for supply chain integrity
- CycloneDX SBOM generation for component transparency
- CVE scanning integration (e.g., Trivy, Snyk) for vulnerability detection
- Gatekeeper/OPA policy for runtime enforcement
- Canary deployments and rollback strategies in multi-cloud contexts

## Code Example

### GitHub Actions Workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yaml`)
```yaml
name: Image Provenance Gate
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  build-scan-sign:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
      - name: Build and push image
        run: |
          docker build -t ghcr.io/org/app:${{ github.sha }} .
          docker push ghcr.io/org/app:${{ github.sha }}
      
      - name: Generate CycloneDX SBOM
        uses: cyclonedx/ghcr-create-sbom@v1
        with:
          format: json
          output-file: sbom.json
      
      - name: Run CVE scan
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@master
        with:
          image-ref: 'ghcr.io/org/app:${{ github.sha }}'
          format: json
          exit-code: '1'
          severity: 'CRITICAL,HIGH'
      
      - name: Sign image with Cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3
        with:
          cosign-version: 'v2'
      - name: Sign image
        run: |
          cosign sign --yes ghcr.io/org/app:${{ github.sha }}
      
      - name: Generate SBOM with Syft
        run: |
          syft ghcr.io/org/app:${{ github.sha }} -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.json
```

### Gatekeeper Policy (`constraint-template.yaml`)
```yaml
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: requirecosignsignature
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: RequireCosignSignature
      targets:
        - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
          rego: |
            package requirecosignsignature
            violation["image is not signed with Cosign"] {
              image := input.review.object.spec.containers[_].image
              notcosign.verify(image)
            }
```

### Failing Manifest (Unsigned Image)
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: unsigned-app
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: ghcr.io/org/app:unsigned-latest
    ports:
    - containerPort: 8080
```

### Passing Manifest (Signed Image)
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: signed-app
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: ghcr.io/org/app:v1.0.0
    ports:
    - containerPort: 8080
```

### Verification Steps
```bash
# Verify image signature
cosign verify ghcr.io/org/app:v1.0.0

# Verify SBOM exists
cosign verify-attestation --type cyclonedx ghcr.io/org/app:v1.0.0

# Verify against Gatekeeper policy
kubectl get requirecosignsignature
```

Why This Is Asked

Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-secure-deployments
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  background: true
  rules:
  - name: security-context
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment"]

      message: "Each container must define a secure securityContext with runAsNonRoot: true, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, and drop all capabilities"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - securityContext:
                  runAsNonRoot: "true"
                  readOnlyRootFilesystem: "true"
                  capabilities:
                    drop: ["ALL"]
  - name: require-resources
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment"]
    validate:
      message: "Each container must specify resource limits and requests"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - resources:
                  limits:
                    memory: "?*"
                    cpu: "?*"
                  requests:
                    memory: "?*"
                    cpu: "?*"
```

    cosign verify --key "$PUBKEY" "$img" || { echo "Unsigned: $img"; exit 1; }
  done
done
```

## Code Example

```yaml
name: prod-provenance
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - manifests/prod/**
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: setup cosign
        run: |
          curl -sSfL https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/releases/download/v1.10.0/cosign-linux-amd64 -o cosign
          chmod +x cosign
          sudo mv cosign /usr/local/bin/
      - name: verify images

          cyclone_dx_attest --image registry.example.com/namespace/service:tag --attest

- Kubernetes NetworkPolicy basics
- Namespace-scoped policy enforcement

## Code Example

# Passing manifest (NetworkPolicy for team-a)
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-ingress
  namespace: team-a
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
```

name: Namespace NetworkPolicy Gate
on:

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
